name: PixiTween Director S16b: cartoon crew (cast, set, motion, blocking into stage3d, critic, forge lane)
description: Gives the Muse crew a toy-studio workflow: the showrunner casts characters, dresses the set, requests motion and dispatches one blocking job per shot that writes an engine stage3d layer with a locked camera; the critic checks character, product and intersections on captured frames; the studio shows a forge lane. Catalog fan-out (S15) swaps the product glTF per product on top.

userStories.title: Cartoon contracts: job kinds, storyboard beats and cues, cartoon events
userStories.description: As a crew member, I want job kinds, shot cues and events for the toy studio so that the board, the replay and the UI show cartoon work like any other job.
steps: Read shared/crew.ts (JOB_KINDS, priorities), shared/storyboard.ts (sceneSchema) and shared/events.ts.
Edit shared/crew.ts: add 'cast-character', 'make-prop', 'make-set', 'make-motion' and 'block-shot' to JOB_KINDS; block-shot is a writing kind; the forge kinds are not; add lane 'forge' to LANES.

Edit shared/storyboard.ts: scenes get optional beats (≤ 300 chars), castIds string[], cues [{ atSec, actorId, clip, mark?: [x, z, facingDeg] }] and lightCue?: 'dawn' | 'studio' | 'spotlight' | 'night'.
Edit shared/events.ts: add forge.job { job } and cast.updated { member } events.
Add or extend shared tests.
acceptanceCriteria: A scene with cues [{ atSec: 1.5, actorId: 'c1', clip: 'wave', mark: [0, 0, 0] }] parses
JOB_KINDS contains 'block-shot' and WRITING_KINDS contains it; WRITING_KINDS does not contain 'cast-character'
A forge.job event parses through the FilmEvent schema

userStories.title: Casting worker: concept art → mask → rigged character
userStories.description: As a showrunner, I want a cast-character job to turn a character description into a rigged toy character so that the film has a mascot that can act.
steps: Read server/art/* (Muse Image generation, prompt lint, SAM 3.1 cut-out) and server/forge/client.ts.

Create server/cartoon/casting.ts exporting runCastJob(job, signal, crew): generate one concept image with Muse Image using the template 'a cute vinyl toy figure of <description>, full body, A-pose, arms away from body, plain light grey background, soft studio light' (prompt-linted), cut it out with SAM 3.1 (noun 'toy figure'), call forge.character(image, mask), wait, store the rig asset, update FilmState.cast and emit cast.updated and forge.job.
On a forge failure set the member status 'failed' with the error and push an inbox item to the showrunner.
Map 'cast-character' in server/crew/workers/registry.ts.
Add server/cartoon/casting.test.ts with the fake forge and recorded Muse Image/SAM fixtures.
acceptanceCriteria: A cast job for 'a round orange fox' ends with one cast member status 'rigged' and a rig asset
The Muse Image prompt contains 'A-pose' and the description, and no brand term passes the lint
A forge failure leaves the member 'failed' and puts exactly one inbox item

userStories.title: Set and prop workers: backdrop, props and the product in 3D
userStories.description: As a set dresser, I want a painted toy-diorama backdrop and 3D props and product so that the shot has a world to stand in.
steps: Read server/art/* (generatePlate), server/forge/client.ts and the stage3d set/props schema in aep-31 requirements.

Create server/cartoon/set.ts exporting runSetJob: one Muse Image backdrop in the style 'miniature toy diorama of <place>, tilt-shift, soft daylight, no characters' at 16:9, stored as FilmState.set.backdropAssetId.
Create server/cartoon/props.ts exporting runPropJob: one Muse Image prop image ('a single toy <noun>, plain background'), SAM 3.1 mask, forge.object, mesh asset into FilmState.set.props.
Export runProductJob: SAM 3.1 mask of the film's product photo → forge.object → FilmState.productMeshAssetId (add the field in shared/composition.ts only if S16a has not).
Map 'make-set' and 'make-prop' in the registry; the product mesh runs as a 'make-prop' with productOf set.
Add server/cartoon/set.test.ts and props.test.ts with fakes.
acceptanceCriteria: A set job stores one backdrop asset and its prompt contains 'diorama' and no character words
A prop job for 'teapot' adds one prop with a mesh asset
The product job uses the film's product photo, not a generated image (the fake records the photo asset id)

userStories.title: Motion worker: library clip by name or act-it-out video
userStories.description: As an animator, I want a make-motion job to supply a named clip so that blockers can cue it on any character.
steps: Read scripts/forge/import-clips.ts (clip-library.json) and server/forge/client.ts motionVideo.

Create server/cartoon/motion.ts exporting resolveClip(name) from the library (exact, then a small synonym table: hello→wave, celebrate→jump, show→present), and runMotionJob: library hit → FilmState.clips entry with source 'library'; a job with an uploaded video → forge.motionVideo → clip asset with source 'video'.
Map 'make-motion' in the registry.

Create server/cartoon/routes.ts with registerCartoonRoutes(app, deps) adding POST /api/films/:id/act (multipart video ≤ 30 s, passcode) that queues a make-motion job named by the form field 'name'; edit server/http/routes.ts to call it.
Add server/cartoon/motion.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: resolveClip('hello') returns the library clip named 'wave'
A make-motion job with a video produces one clip with source 'video' via the fake forge
POST /act with a 40-second video returns 400 naming the 30 s limit

userStories.title: Stage authoring tools: stage3d per scene with locked camera
userStories.description: As a blocker, I want authoring tools that write a stage3d layer for a scene so that a shot is built from validated, versioned edits.
steps: Read server/tools/authoring.ts (runAuthoring, films.mutate), server/authoring/api.ts and the aep-31 stage3d schema from the engine package.
Edit server/env.ts and .env.example: CARTOON_MODE boolOff with a one-line comment.

Create server/cartoon/stage-api.ts (pure): addStage(comp, sceneId, { backdropAssetId, lightPreset, style }) adds one stage3d layer under the scene's 2D title layers with a fixed camera (position [0, 1.4, 6], target [0, 0.9, 0], fov 35); placeActor(comp, sceneId, actorId, assetId, mark); cueClip(comp, sceneId, actorId, clipAssetId, atFrame, opts); moveActor(comp, sceneId, actorId, toMark, atFrame, durationFrames); placeProp(...); placeProduct3D(...); setLightCue(comp, sceneId, cue) mapping dawn/studio/spotlight/night to key/fill/rim keyframes.

Edit server/tools/authoring.ts to expose these as tools (addStage, placeActor, cueClip, moveActor, placeProp, placeStageProduct, setLightCue), each validated by the engine schema; when CARTOON_MODE is on, setCamera accepts only 'static'.
Edit server/agent/storyboard.ts so the storyboard camera enum is ['static'] when CARTOON_MODE is on.
Add server/cartoon/stage-api.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: addStage then placeActor then cueClip produces a composition that the engine's parseAepComposition accepts at schema 1.11.0
No tool can produce a stage3d camera with keyframes (a test tries and gets a validation error)
setLightCue('dawn') produces a key light intensity keyframe that rises from 0 at the scene start

userStories.title: Blocking worker: one Spark builder per shot writes the stage
userStories.description: As a showrunner, I want one block-shot job per scene so that shots are staged in parallel from the beats and cues.
steps: Read server/crew/workers/builder.ts (scope guard, tool loop) and server/cartoon/stage-api.ts.

Create server/cartoon/blocking.ts exporting runBlockJob: builds the scene from storyboard beats, castIds and cues using only the stage tools plus setText/restyleText for titles; scope-guarded to its own scene; prompt in server/cartoon/prompts.ts states the rules (locked camera; actors on the 3×3 stage grid x ∈ {-1.5, 0, 1.5}, z ∈ {-1, 0, 1}; product never covered by an actor; every cue must use a clip that exists).
Map 'block-shot' in the registry.
Add server/cartoon/blocking.test.ts with a scripted Spark backend.
acceptanceCriteria: A scripted block job for scene s2 changes only s2's precomp (s1 and s3 JSON unchanged)
A cue naming a clip that is not in FilmState.clips makes the tool call fail and the job retry with the error, then succeed with an existing clip

Create server/cartoon/showrunner-tools.ts: castCharacter({ name, description }), dressSet({ place, props: string[] ≤ 4 }), requestMotion({ name, from: 'library' | 'act' }), blockShot({ sceneId }) and lightCue({ sceneId, cue }); dependencies: blockShot refuses while the scene's cast, props or clips are not ready and says which.

Edit server/crew/showrunner-tools.ts to append them when CARTOON_MODE is on; edit server/crew/prompts.ts to add the toy-studio section from server/cartoon/prompts.ts (order: cast + set + motion in parallel, then block shots, then review; locked camera; 3 actors max).
Edit server/crew/fake-showrunner.ts to delegate to a scripted cartoon turn when CARTOON_MODE is on (fixture character, cube prop, wave clip, 3 shots).
Add server/cartoon/showrunner-tools.test.ts.

The fake cartoon run with DIRECTOR_FAKE=1 ends with 3 blocked scenes and status 'ready', with 0 Meta or forge network calls

userStories.title: Critic checks for cartoon shots
userStories.description: As a viewer, I want the critic to catch a character out of frame, a hidden product or a limb through a prop so that the film looks finished.
steps: Read server/crew/workers/critic.ts (blind review, findings) and server/review/rules-core.ts.

Create server/cartoon/checks.ts: rules computed from the stage JSON at the captured times (actor mark outside the camera's visible ground area; product screen box overlapped > 40% by an actor's box; two actors closer than 0.6 units) and a blind vision question list for Spark ('Is any character's body passing through an object? Is the main product clearly visible? Is any character cut off by the frame edge?').
Feed these findings into the existing critic flow for scenes that contain a stage3d layer; each finding names the scene, second and actor.
Add server/cartoon/checks.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: An actor marked at x = 4 with the default camera yields one 'actor-off-frame' finding
An actor box covering 60% of the product box yields one 'product-covered' finding naming the actor

readFirst: reacthub-pixitweenjs specs/features/aep-31-stage3d/requirements.md (the stage3d layer the blockers write)
metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Every story is implementable and verifiable with unit tests, recorded fixtures and the browser preview; nothing here spends money or needs network. Live and paid checks are listed in metadata.manualGates and run by the owner.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use recorded fixtures and DIRECTOR_REPLAY=1. Never call Meta, Clippy, Ollama or any other network service from a story, a test or a script you run during a story. The only network use allowed is `npm install`.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.
For engine behaviour (composition JSON, Player, timeline, layer kinds) read docs/engine/README.md before writing code; never edit or copy engine source.

Never edit anything under node_modules/. The engine `reacthub-pixitweenjs` is a dependency: if it lacks something, add a row to ENGINE-NEEDS.md (what, where, proposed API, workaround, story) and use a workaround or set notes to 'blocked: engine'.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests. Files under shared/ are contracts (specs/hackathon/meta/06-contracts.md): change them only in a story that says so.
Never put keys, tokens, cookies or personal data in code, fixtures, logs or docs. Fixtures are redacted: no Authorization headers and no data: URLs longer than 200 characters.
No real brand names, logos or real people's likeness in prompts, fixtures or assets.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements, latencies, prices or test output.
Do not add a dependency that the story or 06-contracts.md does not name. If one is truly needed, say why in notes.
Debug output goes to debug/<step>/iteration-NN/ (gitignored). Only curated, redacted fixtures are committed, under fixtures/<step>/.

A step that would call a paid or live API is written as a script that prints an estimate and exits unless `--yes` is passed (`npm run live -- <step> --yes`, one file per step under scripts/live/). Create such scripts; never run them.
The camera is locked: blockers never write camera keyframes, and setCamera accepts only 'static' when CARTOON_MODE is on.
Blocking is deterministic JSON authoring through tools validated against the engine schema; a blocker never writes composition JSON by hand.
No real brand names, logos or the LEGO name or minifigure shape in prompts, fixtures or concept art.
Needs engine 0.3.0-alpha.6 (aep-31). Until it is published, link the engine with ENGINE_SPEC=file:../reacthub-pixitweenjs; never copy engine source.

ui: Verify in the browser (dev-browser skill or preview): `npm run dev`, open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, and record what you saw in `notes`

manualGates: MG-1: owner publishes reacthub-pixitweenjs 0.3.0-alpha.6 (aep-31 validation passed) and bumps the engine here.
MG-2: owner runs `npm run live -- s16-cartoon` then `--yes` with the product photo fixture: one cartoon film end to end; records wall time, cost (models + GPU), critic findings and fixes.
MG-3: owner records a 3-second 'wave' on a phone and runs the act-it-out flow once; checks the mascot's wave in the film.
